story_title: As Venue Staff, I want to maintain venue information so that Event Coordinators can identify venues that meet event requirements

acceptance_criteria.text: Venue Staff can create a venue record.
Venue information includes location, capacity, facilities and accessibility information.
Supported room layouts can be recorded, each with its own capacity value.
Venue operating information can be recorded.
Authorised users can update venue information.
Unavailable or inactive venues are not presented as available options.
When a venue's attributes are updated or it is retired, existing bookings that may be affected are flagged for review rather than automatically changed, and the assigned Coordinator is notified.

Logged in as Venue Staff: marcus.wong@connectsphere.com / password123

Enter a reason in the confirmation dialog

Logged in as Venue Staff: marcus.wong@connectsphere.com / password123

Venue: Test Meeting Room (TEST-01)

test_cases.title: Reducing a layout below an approved booking's attendance flags that booking

Demo data freshly loaded — no flag can be cleared from the app, so reload the demo data before this test.
One-North Seminar Room (ONE-SEM) seats 80 theatre-style and has one approved future booking: 'Tanjong Legal CPD Seminar' on 28 Oct 2026, whose event expects 70 people. Its coordinator is Joel Fernandez.
Logged in as Venue Staff: marcus.wong@connectsphere.com / password123
steps: Open 'One-North Seminar Room' from the Venues list
Change the Theatre layout's Seats value
test_cases.test_data: Theatre seats: change 80 to 60 (the event expects 70)
test_cases.expected_result:

It states the bookings have NOT been changed and that each is flagged for its coordinator to decide what to do.
It lists 'Tanjong Legal CPD Seminar: the booked layout no longer seats the expected attendance'.

open_questions: AC7 says the assigned Coordinator is notified, but there is no notifications screen in the application. The top-bar bell and every sidebar 'Notifications' link point at a page that does not exist yet, so a tester can see the confirmation that coordinators were notified but cannot open a coordinator's inbox to verify it. Is building that screen part of SPM-39, or a separate story?

AC7 says affected bookings are 'flagged for review', but nothing in the application shows the flag once the save confirmation has gone. There is no review queue and no flag indicator on any booking screen, so the flag is only visible in the database. How should a tester verify that a flag persists?

Nothing can clear a flag once set — that was scoped out as a follow-up story. Every AC7 test therefore leaves permanent state, so the demo data has to be reloaded between runs. Is that acceptable for the test cycle, or should the acknowledge/resolve story be pulled into SPM-39?

AC7 says 'existing bookings that may be affected'. The implementation treats only approved bookings that have not yet finished as candidates: pending, rejected, cancelled and already-finished bookings are never flagged. TC20 and TC21 test it this way — please confirm it matches the intent of discussion #120 and #122.

AC7 also says bookings are not 'automatically changed'. A tester cannot confirm this independently, because no screen shows a booking's venue, layout, times or status — the Booking Requests screen is not built. Currently the only evidence is the wording of the confirmation panel. Is that enough, or should verification wait for the bookings screen?

AC6 covers both 'unavailable' and 'inactive' venues, but only the inactive half is testable. Retired venues are excluded from the Coordinator's catalogue (TC15). The venue search and booking request screens that would 'present available options' are not built, and venue unavailability (maintenance blocks) has no screen either, so the 'unavailable' half cannot be exercised. Is AC6 considered satisfied for this story?

A layout's capacity is allowed to exceed the venue's maximum capacity, and the demo data relies on it — Jurong Training Room has a Theatre layout of 70 against a maximum capacity of 60. Intended, or should the form reject a layout larger than the room?
The rule that a closing time must be after the opening time is only enforced in the browser (TC11). The API itself accepts a venue that closes before it opens. Should the server reject it too?

Narrowing a venue's opening hours is deliberately not treated as an impact yet, so a booking that now falls outside the opening hours is NOT flagged. This was deferred because comparing the stored opening time text against a booking's date and time needs a timezone convention the codebase has not settled. Please confirm this is acceptable for SPM-39 rather than a gap in AC7.
AC2 mentions 'accessibility information'. This is implemented as accessibility tick boxes only; unlike an event, a venue has no free-text accessibility notes field. Is the tick list sufficient?

Duplicate layout names are rejected by the server, but the layout picker only ever offers layouts that are not already used, so the rejection cannot be reached from the interface. TC09 tests the picker instead. No test covers the server-side rule.
